title: Strict-system realization and composition coherence of integral pullback comparisons
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed algebraic closure, with valuation rings $\mathcal O_F$, uniformizers $\varpi_F$ and $A_{F,n}=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n$ for $F=E,L$ and $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $h:Z\to W$ and $k:W\to V$ be scheme morphisms, with $\ell$ invertible on these schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the completed coefficient sheaves $R_{F,U}=\varprojlim_n(A_{F,n})_U$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], the derived-complete constructible categories $\mathcal C_F(U)=D^b_c(U,\mathcal O_F)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the completed pullbacks $F_{f,F}=Lf_F^*$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], and the strict-tower scalar extensions $T_U=T_{L/E,U}$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. The finite module pullbacks use the canonical constant-coefficient identifications and the termwise composition maps $c_{h,k,n}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Realization means the functor $R\lim$ on the derived category of strict towers, or its $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ model on the quotient complexes [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit, def-pur-integral-derived-operations].

The following construction specifies comparison families, including the identifications used in their realization. For $K\in\mathcal C_E(V)$ take a flat-term K-flat representative $P\to K$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and its simultaneous quotients $P_{F,n}=P\otimes_{R_{E,V}}(A_{F,n})_V$. For any such scheme map $f:U\to U'$ use the same notation for a representative $P$ on its target $U'$, and set
$$Q_{f,F}(P)_n=f^*P_{F,n},\qquad Q_{h,k,E}(P)_n=h^*k^*P_{E,n}.$$
Transitions are induced by the actual quotient maps, and restriction of scalars to the relevant completed coefficient sheaf is implicit. There are natural comparison isomorphisms
$$\eta_{h,k,K}:F_{h,E}F_{k,E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim Q_{h,k,E}(P),$$
$$\lambda_{f,K}:T_UF_{f,E}K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim Q_{f,L}(P),\qquad
\mu_{f,K}:F_{f,L}T_VK\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim Q_{f,L}(P).$$
These comparisons use the derived-limit counit of the entire tower, with the following precise normalization. Write $\Delta$ for the constant-tower functor. For a strict tower complex $C_\bullet$, take a K-injective tower resolution $C_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex] and define
$$\epsilon_C:\Delta R\lim C_\bullet\longrightarrow C_\bullet\quad\text{in }D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R)))$$
by the ordinary limit-cone map $\Delta\lim I_\bullet\to I_\bullet$, transported through that resolution. Here $R$ is the completed coefficient sheaf at the relevant scheme; this specifies the counit without discarding tower homotopies. Apply derived change of rings levelwise to this counit, then the quotient-module action maps (the counits of extension/restriction of scalars) and the tensor associators [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The resulting arrows are taken in the derived category of the whole quotient diagram. In detail, $\eta$ is the realization of $h^*$ applied to the resulting arrow from the $A_{E,\bullet}$-reduction tower of $F_{k,E}K$ to $k^*P_{E,\bullet}$; $\lambda$ is realization of the resulting arrow from the $A_{L,\bullet}$-coefficient tower of $F_{f,E}K$ to $f^*P_{L,\bullet}$, using $(f^*P_{E,n})\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{L,n}\cong f^*P_{L,n}$; $\mu$ is realization of $f^*$ applied to the resulting arrow from the $A_{L,\bullet}$-reduction tower of $T_VK$ to $P_{L,\bullet}$. The reduction and scalar towers here are precisely those of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations, def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. The initial completion map from an uncompleted K-flat representative to its quotient cone has the quotient-map component in the unshifted product and zero component in the shifted product. The counit construction, rather than arbitrary individual reduction isomorphisms, supplies all iterated identifications. These constructions descend independently of the tower resolutions, K-flat representatives and common refinements, and the displayed $\eta,\lambda,\mu$ are isomorphisms. Put
$$c^E_{h,k,K}=\eta_{h,k,K}^{-1}\circ R\lim(c_{h,k,\bullet}):F_{kh,E}K\longrightarrow F_{h,E}F_{k,E}K,$$
$$a_{f,K}=\mu_{f,K}^{-1}\circ\lambda_{f,K}:T_UF_{f,E}K\longrightarrow F_{f,L}T_VK.$$
The source in the first formula is identified with $R\lim Q_{kh,E}(P)$ by the defining pullback construction. These formulas give natural isomorphisms and specify the choices of the integral composition and pullback scalar comparisons whose existence is asserted in [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition, lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. The analogous formula defines $c^L$.

With these specified families the composition/scalar equation is
$$F_{h,L}(a_{k,K})\circ a_{h,F_{k,E}K}\circ T_Z(c^E_{h,k,K})
=c^L_{h,k,T_VK}\circ a_{kh,K}.$$
The composition maps are associative and unital, and these equations respect equality of scheme morphisms and arbitrary finite iterations. For $E=L$ the scalar comparison is the identity under multiplication and completeness. For $E\subset L\subset M$, the comparisons respect the integral scalar associator obtained by conjugating the ordinary derived tensor associator by the specified completion maps $\chi$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. All the asserted equations are equalities of the transformations of simultaneous quotient diagrams before realization, transported by the displayed comparison maps. Their rationalizations give the same equations in the raw rationalized constructible categories [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. No finite Tor-amplitude hypothesis on the finite reductions is imposed.

source.place: Tag 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (2),(5), completed pullback and quotient realization; with Tag 0D6D, sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-derived-pullback-composition. The simultaneous integral scalar/composition coherence is an extracted construction, not a verbatim assertion of either tag; blueprint prop-trf-karoubi-independence.proof.md, last sentence.

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat representative P→K by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Form the quotient complexes P_{F,n}=P⊗_{R_{E,V}}(A_{F,n})_V and their actual quotient transitions, and pull them back termwise to define Q_{f,F}(P) and Q_{h,k,E}(P). The definitions of completed pullback and scalar extension in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] and [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], together with [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], identify these with the required finite-level derived constructions. The reduction isomorphisms in [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] (1) and the coherent quotient-system model in [lem-pur-coefficient-extension-reduction-model] show that these are strict normalized towers, including the scalar tower, with transitions induced by the actual quotient maps.

source.place: Tags 06YS, 06YT and 06YY; termwise derived change of rings and derived pullback

proof.text: For a strict tower C_• take a K-injective tower resolution C_•→I_• and use the ordinary limit-cone map Δ lim I_•→I_•. The strict-tower homotopy-limit theorem [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] says that this construction is the total derived inverse limit, is functorial on tower maps, and has the Roos triangle. Thus ε_C is a morphism in the derived category of the whole tower, rather than a collection of unrelated maps after reduction.

source.place: Tag 0941, derived inverse-limit cone and functoriality

proof.text: Towers of modules over the completed coefficient sheaf (resp. over the quotient rings A_{F,•}) are the modules over the corresponding sheaf of rings on the product of the site with the poset N^op, so [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] applies to the levelwise change of rings R→A_{F,•} on tower derived categories; a constant tower of a K-flat complex is K-flat there, since tensor products and acyclicity are levelwise. Apply ε to the reduction tower of F_{k,E}K and then apply h^*, with the levelwise change-of-rings counits and tensor associators; this gives η_{h,k,K}. Apply the same construction to the L-coefficient tower of F_{f,E}K and to the tower of T_VK after f^*; these give λ_{f,K} and μ_{f,K}. The finite pullback comparison is the canonical termwise map on K-flat reductions by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Its levelwise reduction maps are the canonical isomorphisms supplied by [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] (1), while [lem-pur-coefficient-extension-reduction-model] identifies the scalarized reductions with the L-coefficient quotient tower and supplies their coherent counit. Hence η, λ and μ are maps of the whole strict towers with levelwise isomorphisms; functoriality and exactness of Rlim from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] make them isomorphisms after realization.

source.place: Tags 0941 and 0D6D; realization of finite pullback maps

proof.text: The maps just constructed are independent of P, of the tower resolution, and of common refinements. [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined] gives the unique comparison for completed pullback realizations from two K-flat resolutions, and [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined] gives the analogous comparison for scalar-extension towers. The comparison maps commute with the quotient maps by the tensor formulas in [lem-pur-coefficient-extension-reduction-model] and [lem-pur-scalar-extension-tower-coherence]. Functoriality of Rlim then transports ε, η, λ and μ across these comparisons, proving independence before the families are fixed.

source.place: Tags 06YS, 06YT and 0941; resolution independence of derived-limit constructions

proof.text: Define c^E_{h,k,K}=η_{h,k,K}^{-1}∘Rlim(c_{h,k,•}) and a_{f,K}=μ_{f,K}^{-1}∘λ_{f,K}, and define c^L similarly. The source of c^E is identified with Rlim Q_{kh,E}(P) by the defining pullback tower. Each c_{h,k,n} is the finite canonical composition map, and [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] identifies its strict termwise realization; [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] (1) supplies the reduction isomorphisms used in η, while [lem-pur-coefficient-extension-reduction-model] and [lem-pur-scalar-extension-tower-coherence] supply the scalar-association and quotient-transition maps used in λ and μ. Thus the displayed formulas are valid choices of the comparison families and are natural isomorphisms by Step 3 and functoriality of Rlim. The formula for c^L is applied to T_VK, which lies in D^b_c(V,O_L) by [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible]; likewise T_W F_{k,E}K and T_Z F_{kh,E}K are constructible, so the L-level reduction isomorphisms of [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] (1) apply to all the L-level factors, and the rationalized equations below take place in the rationalized constructible categories.

source.place: Tag 0D6D and Tag 0941; derived composition and total-limit functoriality

proof.text: Before realization, expand the scalar/composition equation using the strict representatives just fixed. First, the counit ε_C of Step 2 is natural in strict tower maps φ:C→C′: lift φ to the K-injective tower resolutions (possible and unique up to homotopy because I′ is K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex]); the ordinary limit-cone maps then commute strictly with the lift. Since levelwise change of rings, the action counits and the termwise pullback h^* are functors on the tower derived categories, the comparison F_{h,L}(R lim C)→R lim h^*C built from ε_C exactly as η is natural in φ, i.e. F_{h,L}(R lim φ) corresponds to R lim(h^*φ). This is what is used below for F_{h,L}(a_{k,K}). The factor a_{k,K} is represented by the strict scalar-association map κ_{k,n}; applying F_{h,L} means applying the termwise pullback h^* to that same tower map, and a_{h,F_{k,E}K} is represented by κ_{h,n}. The factor T_Z(c^E_{h,k,K}) is represented by scalar extension of the finite map c_{h,k,n}, while the right-hand c^L_{h,k,T_VK} and a_{kh,K} use the corresponding L-level composition map and κ_{kh,n}. The strict tower coherence identity [lem-pur-scalar-extension-tower-coherence] and naturality of the finite pullback maps [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] identify the two composites term by term; [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] identifies the tensor reassociations. Applying the functor Rlim from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] gives the displayed equality.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, canonical tensor reassociation; Tag 0941, functorial derived limit

proof.text: The same strict-system calculation with three composable maps gives the two associativity composites of c^E as the same reassociation of (j∘h∘k)^*P_n, and the identity map gives the unit comparison. Equality of scheme morphisms and finite iterations are respected because the finite inverse-image and coefficient maps are functorial, and Rlim preserves these equalities. For E=L, [lem-pur-coefficient-extension-reduction-model] says that the coherent reduction comparison is the usual reduction counit, while [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] identifies χ_{E/E,K} with the derived-completeness map K→Rlim_n(K⊗^L A_{E,n}) after K⊗^L R≅K. Both maps are induced by the same quotient component and zero shifted component, so the specified scalar comparison is the identity under multiplication and completeness.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, associativity and units of canonical pullback comparison

proof.text: For E⊂L⊂M, [lem-pur-coefficient-extension-reduction-model] identifies each scalar reduction comparison with the coherent quotient-system counit, and [lem-pur-scalar-extension-tower-coherence] states that the successive scalar-association maps agree with the direct E⊂M map as strict-system equations. Conjugating the ordinary derived tensor associator by the completion maps χ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] therefore gives the asserted integral scalar associator and its compatibility with all comparisons above. Finally, the scalar-localization functor of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] sends equal strict tower maps to equal rationalized maps, with no finite Tor-amplitude assumption.
